mainTopic: A קרפף next to a courtyard and the מבוי, רבי יוחנן's view of a large קרפף's Torah-level status, and רבה's ruling about bringing water for a מילה on שבת
overview: This amud opens by finishing a rule about a גוי whose courtyard has an opening outside the alley (מבוי). רבה and רב יוסף add a size rule for an opening into a קרפף. A גוי makes the alley אסור if his קרפף is בית סאתים or less, because that is too small for his needs. A ישראל is the reverse: he makes the alley אסור only if his קרפף is larger than בית סאתים, because he may not carry there and will use the alley. Next, רבי יוחנן rules that a large קרפף not fenced for living is still a רשות היחיד by Torah law. רב הונא בר חיננא challenges this from a ברייתא about a rock in the sea, and רבא and רב אשי each defend רבי יוחנן. רב אשי explains that the רבנן balanced two of their own rules and protected the more common case. The amud ends with a story: רבה allows asking a גוי to bring warm water for a baby's מילה. Afterward, אביי begins an objection from a ברייתא that calls both הזאה and אמירה לגוי a שבות, and his objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The rule extends even to an opening into an enclosure
steps.stepSummary: The rule that a גוי's separate opening keeps him from making the מבוי אסור applies even when that opening leads into a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if his opening leads into an enclosure (קרפף).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the rule stated on the previous amud. A גוי's courtyard opening that leads outside the alley counts as his main entrance, even if it leads only into a קרפף. This line also sets up the next step, where רבה and רב יוסף give a size limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case spoke of an opening to a wide-open field. One might think a smaller fenced enclosure is not a real alternative exit. This line says that even a קרפף counts as his main way out, so he still does not make the מבוי אסור for the alley's residents.

keyTerms.meaning: Even (signals the rule stretches further than expected)
An enclosure, usually behind houses, not fenced in for living purposes

phrases.english: Even if it opens into an enclosure.
phrases.notes: Continues the rule on the previous amud: the גוי's separate opening counts as his main entrance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this passage mid-sugya by extending the previous rule about a גוי's separate opening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי whose courtyard opens into a קרפף does not make the מבוי אסור, because that opening is his main entrance.

steps.title: For a gentile, the enclosure's size decides
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף rule that for a גוי, a קרפף of בית סאתים or less does not help, so he makes the מבוי אסור. A larger קרפף does help, so he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה and רב יוסף both say: a גוי with a קרפף of בית סאתים makes the alley אסור. With one larger than בית סאתים, he does not make it אסור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף put a limit on the previous step. For a גוי, the קרפף counts as his main entrance only if it is bigger than בית סאתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is which exit the גוי really uses. A קרפף of בית סאתים or less is too small for all his needs, so his real way out is still the alley, and he makes it אסור. A larger קרפף is enough for him, so the alley is not his main path, and he does not make it אסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Who both say (two אמוראים holding the same view)
An area where two סאה of seed can be sown, about 5,000 square אמות (like the courtyard of the משכן)
Makes carrying אסור for the other residents

phrases.english: It is Rabba and Rav Yosef who both say:
A gentile with an enclosure of two beit se'a renders it prohibited,
phrases.notes: The enclosure is too small for his needs, so he really uses the alley.

phrases.english: More than two beit se'a: he does not render it prohibited.
phrases.notes: The enclosure is enough for him, so it is his main exit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits step 1: a קרפף counts as the גוי's main entrance only above בית סאתים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי with a קרפף of up to בית סאתים makes the מבוי אסור. With a larger קרפף, he does not.

steps.title: For a Jew, the result is reversed
steps.stepSummary: For a ישראל, a קרפף of up to בית סאתים means he does not make the מבוי אסור. A larger קרפף means he does.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ישראל with a קרפף of בית סאתים does not make the alley אסור. With one larger than בית סאתים, he does make it אסור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה and רב יוסף now give the rule for a Jewish courtyard owner. The outcome is the opposite of the rule for a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a ישראל, the question is where he is allowed to carry on שבת. A קרפף of up to בית סאתים is a place he may carry in, so he will carry there and not in the alley, and he does not make it אסור. In a larger קרפף he may not carry, so he will carry by way of the alley, and he makes it אסור unless he joins the עירוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not make carrying אסור for others

steps.whatToRemember: A גוי makes the alley אסור when his קרפף is small (בית סאתים or less). A ישראל makes it אסור when his קרפף is large (more than בית סאתים). The size limit is the same, but the reasons differ. For the גוי, it is about having enough space for his needs. For the ישראל, it is about where he is allowed to carry.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא contradicts itself. The same size gives opposite results because the reasoning is different. A גוי is not bound by שבת, so the only question is which exit he actually uses. A ישראל will carry wherever it is מותר, and carrying is מותר only in a קרפף of up to בית סאתים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea in הלכות עירובין. Whether someone makes the alley אסור depends on where he will realistically use it. That depends on his needs (for a גוי) and on what is מותר for him (for a ישראל).

phrases.english: And a Jew with two beit se'a does not render it prohibited.
phrases.notes: He may carry in this קרפף, so he will not use the alley.

phrases.english: More than two beit se'a: he renders it prohibited.
phrases.notes: Carrying in such a קרפף is אסור, so he will carry by way of the alley.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the statement of רבה and רב יוסף by giving the reverse rule for a ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ישראל with a קרפף of up to בית סאתים does not make the מבוי אסור. With a larger קרפף, he does.

steps.title: רבא בר חקלאי asks about an opening into a קרפף
steps.stepSummary: רבא בר חקלאי asks רב הונא what the law is when the גוי's courtyard also opens into a קרפף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא בר חקלאי asked רב הונא: If the גוי's courtyard has an opening into a קרפף, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A student asks his teacher a direct question: does a גוי's second opening into a קרפף stop him from making the מבוי אסור? This sets up רב הונא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that a separate opening can keep a גוי from making the מבוי אסור. The question here is whether an opening into a קרפף, an enclosed area that is not a home, counts as that kind of separate opening.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a formal question to a teacher)
An enclosed area, like a fenced yard or storage area, that is not used as a home
Open to; has an entrance into

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רָבָא בַּר חַקְלַאי מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rava bar Chaklai asked of Rav Huna:
If it opens into an enclosure, what is the law?
phrases.notes: The subject is the גוי's courtyard, which also opens into the מבוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the same case discussed in steps 1-2 as a formal question to רב הונא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does an opening from the גוי's courtyard into a קרפף keep him from making the מבוי אסור?

steps.title: רב הונא answers that it depends on the size of the קרפף
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא quotes the known rule. A קרפף of בית סאתים or less does not help, so the גוי makes the מבוי אסור. A larger one helps, so he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: They already said that if it is בית סאתים, he makes it אסור. If it is more than בית סאתים, he does not make it אסור.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers by quoting an established rule ('they already said'): the size of the קרפף decides the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small קרפף of up to בית סאתים is not enough for all the גוי's needs, so his real way out is still the מבוי, and he makes it אסור. A bigger קרפף is enough for his needs, so the מבוי is not his main exit, and he does not make it אסור. This matches what רבה and רב יוסף said in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: They have already said (pointing to a known ruling)
An area big enough to plant two סאה of seed, about 5,000 square אמות (like the courtyard of the משכן)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with step 3 about a ישראל. For a ישראל the result is reversed: a small קרפף means he does NOT make the מבוי אסור.

phrases.english: He said to him: They have already said:
If it is two beit se'a, he renders it prohibited;
if it is more than two beit se'a, he does not render it prohibited.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to בית סאתים the גוי makes the מבוי אסור. More than בית סאתים, he does not.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules that a large unfenced-for-living קרפף is a full private domain by Torah law
steps.stepSummary: עולא quotes רבי יוחנן: a קרפף bigger than בית סאתים that was not fenced for living in, even a huge one, is a רשות היחיד by Torah law. Throwing into it from a רשות הרבים makes one חייב, because its walls are real walls. Only living use is missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: A קרפף bigger than בית סאתים that was not fenced for living in, even if it is the size of a כור field or two כור fields, if someone throws into it, he is חייב. Why? It is a real partition. It is only missing residents.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement: רבי יוחנן says a big קרפף is a real רשות היחיד according to the Torah, no matter how large it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on carrying in a large קרפף is only מדרבנן. According to the Torah, the walls make it a full רשות היחיד. What it lacks is people living there, and that is why the רבנן were strict, not because the walls fail to count. So throwing into it from a רשות הרבים is a Torah-level violation that requires a קרבן חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Fenced in for the purpose of living there
A large field size, the area for planting a כור of seed (15 times a בית סאתים)
Liable (here, to bring a קרבן חטאת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main tension of the coming section: is a large enclosed area a רשות היחיד by Torah law, or does size beyond בית סאתים change its status?

phrases.english: Ulla said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
An enclosure larger than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for residence,
even a kor, and even two kor in size,
one who throws into it is liable.
What is the reason? It is a valid partition,
except that it is lacking residents.
phrases.notes: The lack of residents is why the רבנן forbade carrying inside it, but it is still a רשות היחיד by Torah law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the mention of a קרפף larger than בית סאתים and defines its Torah-level status.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרפף larger than בית סאתים, even very large, is a רשות היחיד by Torah law because its walls are valid. Throwing into it makes one חייב.

steps.title: רב הונא בר חיננא challenges from the ברייתא of a rock in the sea
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא cites a ברייתא: a rock in the sea 10 טפחים high and 4 wide is a רשות היחיד, so one may not carry between it and the sea. If smaller, one may carry, but only up to בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא objected: A rock in the sea that is 10 טפחים high and 4 טפחים wide: one may not carry from it to the sea or from the sea to it. If it is smaller than that, one may carry. Up to what size? Up to בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: An objection to רבי יוחנן is brought from a ברייתא. Its exact force is not yet clear, so the גמרא will next work out which part of the ברייתא the size limit refers to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rock 10 high and 4 wide is a רשות היחיד, and the sea is a כרמלית, so carrying between them is forbidden. The ברייתא adds a limit of 'up to בית סאתים'. That seems to suggest an area larger than בית סאתים, which was not fenced for living, is not a real רשות היחיד. That would contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection (from an earlier source)
A rock sticking up out of the sea

phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Chinnana raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: סֶלַע שֶׁבַּיָּם גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה וְרוֹחַב אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: A rock in the sea that is ten handbreadths high and four wide:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין לֹא מִן תּוֹכוֹ לַיָּם
phrases.english: one may not carry, neither from it to the sea
nor from the sea to it.
phrases.notes: The rock is a רשות היחיד and the sea is a כרמלית.

phrases.english: If it is less than this, one may carry.
Up to how much? Up to two beit se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a large area not fenced for living is a Torah-level רשות היחיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts a limit of בית סאתים on the rock, which seems to imply that a larger area is not a רשות היחיד.

steps.title: Which clause does 'up to בית סאתים' refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which part of the ברייתא the limit of בית סאתים is attached to.
steps.simpleTranslation: To which clause does this refer?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to clarify the ברייתא before deciding whether it really challenges רבי יוחנן. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The limit could belong to the first clause (a tall rock that is a רשות היחיד) or to the last clause (a short rock where carrying is allowed). Only if it belongs to the first clause does it seem to contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: To which one? (which clause is meant)

phrases.english: To which clause does it refer?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the ברייתא brought in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'up to בית סאתים' refers to the first clause or the last clause of the ברייתא.

steps.title: The limit cannot refer to the last clause
steps.stepSummary: If the limit referred to the short rock, it would make no sense, because the short rock is a כרמלית like the sea. Carrying between two כרמליות is allowed at any size.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it refers to the last clause: only up to בית סאתים and not more? But he is carrying from a כרמלית to a כרמלית!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first possible reading: the size limit cannot refer to the short rock.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rock less than 10 טפחים high is not a רשות היחיד. It is a כרמלית, just like the sea. Carrying from one כרמלית to another is always allowed, so a size limit there makes no sense. This pushes the limit onto the first clause, which seems to contradict רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (proposing a possibility in order to test it)
The last clause of a teaching
An in-between area, neither private nor public, where the רבנן forbade carrying to or from other domains

steps.confusionAlert: Carrying within a כרמלית, or from one כרמלית to another, is fine. The ban is only on carrying between a כרמלית and a different type of domain.

phrases.english: If you say it refers to the latter clause,
then up to two beit se'a, but not more?
But he is carrying from a karmelit to a karmelit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one answer to the question of step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the reading that 'up to בית סאתים' refers to the last clause of the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A short rock and the sea are both כרמלית. Carrying between two כרמליות is allowed with no size limit, so the limit would make no sense there.

steps.title: The limit must refer to the tall rock, which seems to refute רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: Since the limit cannot refer to the short rock, it must refer to the tall rock. That would mean a tall rock bigger than בית סאתים lets you carry to the sea, so it is a כרמלית. This contradicts רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must refer to the first case, and this is what it means: A rock in the sea that is 10 טפחים high and 4 wide, you may not carry from it to the sea or from the sea to it. Up to what size? Up to בית סאתים. But if it is bigger than בית סאתים, you may carry. So it is a כרמלית. This is a refutation of רבי יוחנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The short rock was ruled out in step 9, so the גמרא attaches the בית סאתים limit to the tall rock. It then uses this reading to refute רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a tall rock bigger than בית סאתים lets you carry between it and the sea, then it is being treated as a כרמלית, just like the sea. A big rock like this is the same as a big קרפף that was not fenced for living. So the ברייתא would show that such a קרפף is a כרמלית, while רבי יוחנן said it is a רשות היחיד by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the only reading left)

steps.confusionAlert: The surprising part is the direction of the rule. Bigger than בית סאתים is MORE lenient here, not less. That leniency is what makes the big rock look like a כרמלית.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not on the first clause,
and this is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: סֶלַע שֶׁבַּיָּם גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה וְרוֹחַב אַרְבָּעָה —
phrases.english: A rock in the sea, ten high and four wide —
one may not carry from it to the sea
nor from the sea into it.
And up to what size? Up to two beit se'a,
but more than two beit se'a — one may carry.
phrases.notes: This isn't said outright; the גמרא is working it out from the two beit se'a limit.

phrases.english: Apparently it is a karmelit,
a refutation of Rabbi Yochanan!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After rejecting the short-rock reading, it adopts the tall-rock reading and completes the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a large unfenced קרפף is a רשות היחיד by Torah law
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A tall rock bigger than בית סאתים lets you carry to the sea, so it is a כרמלית. A large קרפף should then also be a כרמלית.

steps.title: רבא: the limit is about carrying on top of the rock
steps.stepSummary: רבא defends רבי יוחנן. The limit does refer to the tall rock, but it is about carrying on the rock itself. That is allowed only up to בית סאתים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Only someone who does not know how to explain ברייתות raises a refutation against רבי יוחנן. Really it refers to the first case, and this is what it means: but on the rock itself, you may carry. Up to what size? Up to בית סאתים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא rejects the challenge. He re-reads the ברייתא so that the בית סאתים limit is about carrying within the rock, not between the rock and the sea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבא's reading, carrying between the tall rock and the sea is always forbidden, at any size. The size limit only controls carrying on top of the rock. Above בית סאתים, the רבנן limit carrying there to 4 אמות, as with any large קרפף. So nothing here says a big rock is a כרמלית by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Explaining (and smoothing out) ברייתות and משניות
Really / actually (keeps the earlier reading but explains it differently)
Within it, on the rock itself

phrases.english: Rava said:
One who does not know how to explain baraitot —
raises a refutation against Rabbi Yochanan.
Actually it is on the first clause, and this is what it says:
but within it — one may carry.
And up to what size? Up to two beit se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the ברייתא (changing what the limit refers to)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The limit is about carrying between the rock and the sea, so a big rock acts like a כרמלית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The limit is about carrying within the rock. Carrying between the rock and the sea stays forbidden at any size.

steps.title: רב אשי: the limit does refer to rock and sea, but both rules are rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי keeps the reading from the challenge, but says the rule comes from two separate rabbinic rulings. It proves nothing about Torah-level status.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Really it refers to the first case, as you said. But the רבנן said one thing, and they also said another.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a second defense of רבי יוחנן. He accepts that above בית סאתים one may carry between the rock and the sea. The next step explains what he means by his short phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב אשי's view, the leniency of carrying to the sea comes from how the רבנן set up their own decrees. It does not come from the rock being a כרמלית by Torah law. The phrase 'they said, and they said' points to two rabbinic rules that he spells out next.

keyTerms.meaning: They (the rabbis) said this, and they also said that. The same rabbis made both rules.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it is on the first clause,
they said, and they said.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, different answer to the refutation in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The leniency is rabbinic, not Torah-level
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Carrying from a big rock to the sea shows it is truly a כרמלית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission comes from the rabbis' own system of decrees. It says nothing about Torah status.

steps.title: The two rabbinic rules behind רב אשי's answer
steps.stepSummary: Rule one: in a large קרפף not fenced for living, you may carry only 4 אמות. Rule two: you may not carry from a רשות היחיד to a כרמלית. Both are rabbinic.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: a קרפף bigger than בית סאתים that was not fenced for living, you may carry in it only 4 אמות. And they said: you may not carry from a רשות היחיד to a כרמלית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spells out the two rabbinic rules that רב אשי was pointing to. This completes his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules are only rabbinic. Since both come from the same רבנן, they could set them up so that one gives way to the other in a particular case. Steps 14-15 explain exactly how. A leniency inside the rabbinic rules does not change the Torah-level status, so רבי יוחנן still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: A fenced area outside the house, such as a yard or storage enclosure
Four cubits, the small area where carrying is allowed

steps.whatToRemember: Both רבא and רב אשי defend רבי יוחנן. A large קרפף not fenced for living is a רשות היחיד by Torah law. Any treatment of it as a כרמלית is only rabbinic.

phrases.english: They said:
an enclosure greater than two beit se'a
that was not enclosed for residence —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בּוֹ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: one may carry in it only four cubits.
And they said:
one may not carry from a private domain to a karmelit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן אָמְרוּ: קַרְפֵּף יָתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the short phrase of רב אשי in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Spelling out the two rabbinic decrees
steps.terutzMaskana: Since both rules are rabbinic, carrying from a large rock to the sea can be allowed without making it a כרמלית by Torah law.

steps.title: A rock up to בית סאתים: no carrying to or from the sea
steps.stepSummary: If the rock is up to בית סאתים, you may carry all over it. But the רבנן forbade carrying between it and the sea, because it is a full רשות היחיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rock of up to בית סאתים, where one may carry on all of it: the רבנן forbade carrying from the sea onto it or from it into the sea. Why? Because it is a full רשות היחיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is applying the two rabbinic rules from רב אשי to the small rock. Since this rock is a real רשות היחיד, the normal ban on carrying between a רשות היחיד and a כרמלית applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rock up to בית סאתים has no problem for carrying on top of it. It is a complete רשות היחיד. So the usual rabbinic rule kicks in: no carrying between a רשות היחיד and a כרמלית (the sea).

keyTerms.meaning: An area the size of two se'ah of planting, about 5,000 square אמות

phrases.english: A rock of two beit se'a, where it is permitted to carry on all of it,
the Rabbis forbade carrying
neither from the sea into it
nor from it into the sea.
What is the reason?
It is a full private domain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the two rabbinic rules from step 13 to the small rock.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Applying the rabbinic rules to a specific case
steps.terutzMaskana: A small rock is a full רשות היחיד, so carrying between it and the sea is forbidden.

steps.title: A rock bigger than בית סאתים: carrying to the sea allowed
steps.stepSummary: On a rock bigger than בית סאתים, carrying on the whole rock is forbidden. So the רבנן allowed carrying to and from the sea. If they forbade it, people might think the rock is a full רשות היחיד and carry all over it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A rock larger than בית סאתים, where carrying on all of it is forbidden: the רבנן permitted carrying from it to the sea and from the sea to it. Why? Because people might say it is a full רשות היחיד, and then come to carry on all of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the surprising leniency for the big rock. The רבנן relaxed one of their own rules to protect the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both rules here are rabbinic. If the רבנן forbade carrying between the big rock and the sea, people would assume the rock is a real רשות היחיד and freely carry on it. That would break the other rule. So allowing carrying to the sea proves nothing about the rock's Torah-level status, which defends רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will come to (do something)

steps.confusionAlert: The leniency does not mean the big rock is a כרמלית. It is still a רשות היחיד by Torah law. The רבנן allowed carrying only to stop people from carrying on the rock itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the heart of רב אשי's defense of רבי יוחנן. The rule in the ברייתא comes from balancing two rabbinic rules, not from the rock's Torah status.

phrases.english: A rock larger than two beit se'a,
where it is forbidden to carry on all of it,
the Rabbis permitted carrying
from it to the sea and from the sea to it.
What is the reason?
Perhaps people will say:
"It is a full private domain,"
and they will come to carry on all of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵר מִבֵּית סָאתַיִם, דְּאָסוּר לְטַלְטוֹלֵי בְּכוּלֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts the big rock with the small rock from step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rabbinic balancing: one decree is relaxed to protect another
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Allowing carrying to the sea shows the big rock is a כרמלית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The leniency only protects the ban on carrying on the big rock. Its Torah status as a רשות היחיד stays the same.

steps.title: Why favor one rabbinic rule over the other?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the רבנן protected the ban on carrying on the rock instead of the ban on carrying between the rock and the sea.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question that sets up the next step. Both rules are rabbinic, so why did one give way?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rabbinic rules clash. The רבנן chose to keep the ban on carrying on the rock and relax the ban on carrying to the sea. The question asks what reason decides which rule wins.

phrases.english: And what is the difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reasoning given in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ban on carrying on the rock was preferred over the ban on carrying between rock and sea.

steps.title: Carrying on the rock is common; carrying to the sea is rare
steps.stepSummary: People often carry on the rock itself, but rarely carry between the rock and the sea. So the רבנן protected the rule that comes up more often.
steps.simpleTranslation: Carrying within it is common. Carrying from it to the sea and from the sea to it is not common.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. The רבנן chose based on how often each situation happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying on the rock is an everyday thing, so a mistake there would happen often. Carrying between rock and sea is unusual. Giving up the strictness in the rare case to guard the common case makes sense.
steps.whatToRemember: For a rock bigger than בית סאתים, the רבנן allowed carrying to the sea so people would not carry on the rock itself, which happens more often. That protects רבי יוחנן: the rock is still a Torah-level רשות היחיד.

phrases.english: Carrying within it is common.
From it to the sea and from the sea to it —
is not common.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The common case (carrying on the rock) is protected, and the rare case (carrying to the sea) is relaxed.

steps.title: A baby's warm water spills and רבה offers water from his house
steps.stepSummary: A new story starts. A baby's warm water for his ברית מילה spilled on שבת, and רבה said to bring warm water from his own house.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain baby whose warm water spilled. רבה said to them: Let them bring him warm water from my house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new story that leads into a discussion of carrying through a courtyard on שבת. It is setting up אביי's objection in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warm water was needed to wash the baby for his מילה on שבת. רבה wanted it carried from his house, which meant bringing it through a shared courtyard. Whether that is allowed is the issue that comes next.

phrases.english: There was a certain baby
whose warm water spilled.
Rabba said to them:
Let them bring him warm water
from my house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, unrelated to the rock-and-sea discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבה instructed that warm water be brought from his house for the baby's מילה.

steps.title: אביי objects that no עירוב was made
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה: no עירוב חצרות was made, so carrying from the house through the courtyard is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we did not make an עירוב!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's instruction. Without an עירוב, you may not carry from a house into the shared courtyard.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Carrying from a private house into a shared courtyard on שבת needs an עירוב חצרות. אביי points out that none was made, so רבה's plan seems forbidden even though the water is for a מילה.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
But we did not make an eiruv!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא לָא עָרְבִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's instruction from step 18.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's instruction to carry warm water from his house
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Without an עירוב חצרות, carrying from a house into the shared courtyard is forbidden, so the water cannot be brought.

steps.title: רבה suggests relying on the merging of alleyways
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי's challenge by suggesting they rely on a שיתוף מבואות instead of an עירוב חצרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: Let us rely on the שיתוף (the merging of the alleyway).
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge. Even without an עירוב חצרות, he says they can rely on a שיתוף מבואות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שיתוף joins the courtyards of an alleyway together. In a pressing situation like a ברית מילה, it can stand in place of the missing עירוב חצרות. So carrying the water through the courtyard would be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: a merging of the alleyway, which joins its courtyards together for carrying

phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him:
Let us rely on the merging of the alleyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge from step 19 that no עירוב חצרות was made.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative mechanism: a שיתוף מבואות takes the place of the missing עירוב חצרות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an עירוב חצרות, carrying from the house through the courtyard is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: In this pressing case, the שיתוף can serve instead of the עירוב.

steps.title: אביי: No merging was made either
steps.stepSummary: אביי points out that no שיתוף מבואות was made, so רבה's suggestion does not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But we did not make a שיתוף either.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי knocks down רבה's suggestion. There was no שיתוף in this alleyway either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה's answer only works if a שיתוף actually exists. אביי states a fact: nobody made one. So the question returns: how can the water be brought?

keyTerms.meaning: we made a שיתוף (merged the alleyway)

phrases.english: He (Abaye) said to him:
But we did not make a merging.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבה's answer from step 20 on the facts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's suggestion to rely on the שיתוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You cannot rely on a שיתוף that was never made.

steps.title: רבה: Tell a גוי to bring the water
steps.stepSummary: רבה says to have a גוי bring the warm water for the baby.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let them tell a גוי to bring it for him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new solution: ask a non-Jew to bring the water.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling a גוי to do a forbidden act for a Jew on שבת (אמירה לגוי) is normally not allowed. Here רבה permits it for the sake of the מילה. Since the ban is only rabbinic, he treats the need of the ברית as enough reason to allow it.

keyTerms.meaning: telling a non-Jew to do a forbidden act for a Jew on שבת

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying אמירה לגוי is generally allowed on שבת. He allows it here only for the needs of the מילה.

phrases.english: Let them tell a gentile
to bring it for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שיתוף idea fails, רבה offers a different solution.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative permitted method: use a גוי instead of a Jew carrying.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With no עירוב and no שיתוף, there is no way to get the water.
steps.terutzMaskana: A גוי may be asked to bring the water for the מילה.

steps.title: אביי wanted to object but רב יוסף stopped him
steps.stepSummary: אביי reports that he wanted to challenge רבה's ruling, but רב יוסף did not let him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: I wanted to raise an objection against the Master (רבה), but רב יוסף did not let me.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי tells us he had an objection to the גוי ruling but held it back. This sets up the next step, which explains why רב יוסף stopped him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We now know an objection exists, but we do not yet hear what it is. First the גמרא explains the reason for the delay. The content of the objection comes in step 26.

keyTerms.meaning: to raise an objection against him
the Master (a respectful title, here for רבה)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
I wanted to raise an objection against the Master,
but Rav Yosef did not let me,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבה's ruling in step 22 by noting a held-back objection.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי had an objection to the ruling but delayed raising it at רב יוסף's insistence.

steps.title: Rabbinic matters: act first, object later
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's reason comes from רב יהודה's rule: in Torah laws, object before acting. In rabbinic laws, act first and object afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב יוסף said that רב כהנא said: When we were in רב יהודה's house, he would tell us: In a Torah law, we raise the objection and only then act. In a rabbinic law, we act and only then raise the objection.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for why רב יוסף stopped אביי. רב יהודה taught that in rabbinic matters you may act first and discuss the objection afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a Torah law might be broken, the doubt must be settled before anyone acts. If only a rabbinic law is involved, the action may go ahead, and the question is examined later. Since אמירה לגוי is only rabbinic, and the baby needed the water, they brought it first.

keyTerms.meaning: we perform the act (we actually do it)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule of practice: in rabbinic matters, a halachic question does not have to hold up the action. This is especially true when there is a pressing need.

phrases.english: as Rav Yosef said that Rav Kahana said:
When we were in Rav Yehuda's house,
he would say to us:
In a Torah law, we raise the objection
and then we perform the act;
in a rabbinic law, we perform the act
and then we raise the objection.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב יוסף stopping אביי in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: Why רב יוסף would not let אביי object before the water was brought.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב יהודה's teaching, passed on by רב כהנא and רב יוסף.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks what the objection was
steps.stepSummary: Once the water was brought, רב יוסף asks אביי what objection he had wanted to raise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Afterward, he (רב יוסף) said to him: What objection did you want to raise against the Master?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that the act is done, רב יוסף asks אביי to share his objection. This sets up the next step, where אביי states it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows רב יהודה's rule exactly: act first, then examine the objection. The discussion now moves from what to do to whether רבה's ruling was correct.

phrases.english: Afterward, he said to him:
What did you want to object against the Master?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְבָתַר הָכִי אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מַאי בָּעֵית לְאוֹתֹבֵיהּ לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the second half of רב יהודה's rule from step 24: now the objection may be raised.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The content of אביי's objection to רבה's ruling allowing אמירה לגוי.

steps.title: אביי cites a ברייתא: הזאה and אמירה לגוי are both rabbinic
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא that lists הזאה and אמירה לגוי together, both as rabbinic prohibitions (שבות).
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: As it was taught in a ברייתא: Sprinkling (purification water) is a שבות, and telling a גוי is a שבות.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי begins his objection by quoting a ברייתא. The ברייתא puts הזאה and אמירה לגוי in the same group: both are only rabbinic bans.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By grouping the two, the ברייתא suggests they follow the same rules on שבת. On the next amud, אביי draws the comparison: just as הזאה does not override שבת, telling a גוי should not override it either. That would challenge רבה's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: sprinkling the purification water (of the פרה אדומה) on an impure person
a rabbinic prohibition added to protect the rest of שבת
it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: רבה allowed asking a גוי to bring water for a מילה. רב יוסף let it happen first, because in rabbinic matters you act first and object later. Afterward, אביי raised a ברייתא that groups אמירה לגוי with הזאה, both as שבות.

phrases.english: He said to him: As it was taught:
Sprinkling is a rabbinic prohibition,
and telling a gentile is a rabbinic prohibition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's question from step 25 by beginning to state the objection against רבה's ruling in step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The objection rests on a ברייתא that puts אמירה לגוי in the same category as הזאה. Both are שבות, which hints that אמירה לגוי, like הזאה, should not be allowed on שבת.
